entries.name: Lat Pulldown
techniqueCitations: Haff, G. G., & Triplett, N. T. (Eds.). (2016). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (4th ed.). Human Kinetics, pp. 398-399.
Sperandei, S., et al. (2009). Analysis of the execution of lat pull-down exercises. JSCR, 23(7), 2033-2038.
Andersen, V., et al. (2014). Effects of grip width and forearm pronation/supination on muscle activity during the lat pull-down. JSCR, 28(4), 1135-1142.
entries.reason: Redrawn side-on for Entry 0183 (owner): the front view could not show the thing the movement is named for - the elbows driving DOWN to the ribs while the bar travels down in front of the face. Side elevation, seated on the machine seat with the thighs clamped under the pad and the feet flat, the bar seen end-on at the hands on the cable line, and the elbow solved on the drawn shoulder circle per frame (upper 12.5, forearm 12.0) so both bones hold their length on every body. The wrist stays above the elbow throughout and the elbow descends until it finishes below the shoulder. The three grip variants stay front view. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.

frames.caption: Reach long overhead with the arms straight, bar just off its rest.
Set the shoulders down and own the stretch, elbows still high.
The elbows lead: they start down before the bar does.
Elbows leading further down, the bar still high.
Elbows driving down toward the sides, chest staying tall.
The elbows keep descending, the bar following them down.
The bar travels down past the face, torso quiet on the seat.
Elbows past the ribs, forearms angled up to the bar.
Bar reaching the upper chest, elbows below the shoulders.
Hold at the top of the pull, elbows beside the ribs.
Return along the same path, the elbows leading back up.
The bar travels back up past the face under control.
Full reach again, arms long, ready for the next rep.

entries.summary: Thirteen drawn positions of a lat pulldown, seen from the side: seated with the thighs under the pad, the bar travelling down in front of the face to the upper chest, the elbows leading down and finishing below the shoulders beside the ribs.

entries.name: Scapular Pull-Up
techniqueCitations: Haff, G. G., & Triplett, N. T. (Eds.). (2016). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (4th ed.). Human Kinetics, pp. 398-399.
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository after owner review: a pull-up bar is drawn overhead with both hands gripping it, the body hangs straight below it with the feet off the floor, and the shoulder movement reads through the shoulders and the body lifting along the bar - never through shortening the neck, which keeps its drawn length (9 units) in every position. The whole figure translates rigidly, so every drawn segment, the neck included, is exactly constant. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.

frames.caption: Hang with straight arms and let your shoulders rise to your ears.
Set the shoulder blades before anything else moves.
Pull the shoulder blades down and back - the body starts to rise.
The body lifts a few inches; the arms stay straight the whole way.
Hold the top for a beat.
Lower with control back toward the full hang.
Full hang again, still with straight arms.

entries.summary: Seven drawn positions of a scapular pull-up, seen from the front.

entries.name: One Arm Lat Pulldown
techniqueCitations: Video: 'One Arm Lat Pulldown' technique demonstration (YouTube, video ID eM162KNncD8).
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: kneeling square to a high cable with one handle, the working arm reaches long and drives the elbow down toward the hip until the upper arm reaches the ribs, and the other arm rests still on the hip in a stable support position. The torso stays square and quiet while one side works. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.

frames.caption: Reach long at the top; keep the torso square and quiet.
Set the shoulder before the elbow bends.
Start the pull with the shoulder blade.
Drive the elbow down toward the hip.
Keep pulling through the elbow, not the hand.
The torso stays square and quiet.
Pause when the upper arm reaches the ribs.
Begin the return under control.
The reach returns long.
Stay square as the arm extends.
Let the shoulder blade travel.
Almost back to the full reach.
Full reach again; ready for the next rep.

entries.summary: Seven drawn positions of a one-arm lat pulldown from a high cable, seen from the front.

entries.name: Close-Grip Front Lat Pulldown
techniqueCitations: Haff, G. G., & Triplett, N. T. (Eds.). (2016). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (4th ed.). Human Kinetics, pp. 398-399.
Andersen, V., et al. (2014). Effects of grip width and forearm pronation/supination on muscle activity during the lat pull-down. JSCR, 28(4), 1135-1142.
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository after the stock grip re-solve was escalated (a close grip folded the elbow inside the shoulder): the athlete sits at the pulldown machine with the thighs under the pad and pulls with the hands held close together (about 12 units apart against the base movement open grip of about 34), converging slightly as the bar reaches the chest. The elbows are solved on the base movement exact shoulder-root circle. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.

frames.caption: Reach long overhead with the hands close together.
Set the shoulders before the elbows bend.
Pull through the elbows, not the hands.
Keep the hands close as the bar descends.
The elbows drive down toward the ribs.
Chest up to meet the bar; shoulders down and back, not rolled forward. Pause here, then let the bar rise under control.
Chest up to meet the bar; shoulders down and back, not rolled forward. Pause here, then let the bar rise under control.
Chest up to meet the bar; shoulders down and back, not rolled forward. Pause here, then let the bar rise under control.
The reach returns long.
Stay tall as the arms extend.
Keep the hands close on the way up.
Almost back to the full reach.
Full reach again; ready for the next rep.

entries.summary: Thirteen drawn positions of a close-grip lat pulldown, seen from the front.

entries.name: Underhand Cable Pulldowns
techniqueCitations: Haff, G. G., & Triplett, N. T. (Eds.). (2016). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (4th ed.). Human Kinetics, pp. 398-399.
Andersen, V., et al. (2014). Effects of grip width and forearm pronation/supination on muscle activity during the lat pull-down. JSCR, 28(4), 1135-1142.
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing was against this text: the hands were wider than the shoulders. Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 40 degrees so the narrow grip and the lean both show: seated under a high pulley with the thighs under the knee pad, leaning back slightly, hands closer than shoulder width on the bar and arms straight; the bar is pulled to the upper chest as the elbows travel down and back beside the ribs, a squeeze, and a slower return to straight arms. The trunk and legs do not move. Not drawn: the palms-facing-you grip.
entries.summary: Seated at a pulldown with a narrow underhand grip and a slight lean back, pull the bar to the upper chest with the elbows close to the body, squeeze, then let it rise slowly.

frames.caption: Sit at a pulldown station with the knee pad snug, take the bar with the palms facing you and the hands closer than shoulder width, and lean back slightly with the chest up.
Keeping the elbows close to the body, draw the shoulders and upper arms down and back to pull the bar to the upper chest.
Squeeze the back. Chest up to meet the bar.
Let the bar rise slowly until the arms are straight.
Elbows close to the body. Return slowly to a full reach.

entries.name: V-Bar Pullup
techniqueCitations: Haff, G. G., & Triplett, N. T. (Eds.). (2016). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (4th ed.). Human Kinetics, pp. 398-399.
Andersen, V., et al. (2014). Effects of grip width and forearm pronation/supination on muscle activity during the lat pull-down. JSCR, 28(4), 1135-1142.
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing was against this text: the hands were apart on the bar. Source-bound side-view draft: both hands on one V-handle hung over the middle of the bar, which is seen end-on; the body hangs on straight arms leaning back slightly, and is pulled up until the chest is close to the handle with the head passing behind the bar, a pause, and a slower lowering to a full hang. The hands do not move.
entries.summary: Hanging from a V-handle over the middle of the bar, leaning back slightly, pull up until the chest is close to the handle, pause, then lower slowly to a full hang.

frames.caption: Hang a V-handle over the middle of the pull-up bar, grip one side in each hand and hang with the arms straight, chest up and leaning back slightly.
Pull the body up, leaning the head back slightly to clear the bar, until the chest is close to the handle.
Pause. Pull through the elbows.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
Chest up, lean back slightly.

entries.name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
entries.summary: Thirteen drawn positions of a wide-grip lat pulldown, seen from the front.
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository after owner review: the seat is set low so the athlete reads seated - hips just above the knee line, thighs foreshortened under the pad (declared projection), shins full and vertical, feet flat on the floor - while the wide grip (hands 41.7 apart at the pause, against the base Lat Pulldown's 33.7) stays clearly visible. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.

frames.caption: Reach long with the hands wide on the bar.
Set the shoulders before the elbows bend.
Pull through the elbows, not the hands.
Keep the hands wide as the bar descends.
The elbows drive down toward the ribs.
Keep the torso tall and the sit square.
Chest up to meet the bar; shoulders down and back, not rolled forward. Pause here, then let the bar rise under control.
Let the bar rise under control.
The reach returns long.
Stay square as the arms extend.
Keep the hands wide on the way up.
Almost back to the full reach.
Full reach again; ready for the next rep.
